skill.name: routeros-sniffer
skill.description: Guides authorized RouterOS packet capture, TZSP streaming, pcap saving, and host-side receiver setup for network protocol debugging.
skill.summary: Set up authorized RouterOS packet captures and TZSP receivers for network debugging.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: The strongest confirmed issues are privileged firewall-change commands and security-sensitive packet mirroring guidance. Most static hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholders, private lab IPs, temporary capture paths, or documentation links. No evidence of prompt injection was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before sudo firewall changes, scope rules to trusted interfaces when possible, and include rollback steps beside every rule.
Mark these as lab-only examples, recommend HTTPS when available, and use a least-privilege account instead of the default admin account.
Add authorization and data-handling warnings before capture workflows, and recommend narrow filters that avoid unnecessary payload collection.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Packet Capture and Mirroring Capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill teaches agents to stream live packets, save pcap files, and mirror selected flows to a remote TZSP receiver. This is legitimate for authorized debugging, but it can expose payloads, credentials, and private network metadata if misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple sections explicitly describe live packet streaming, pcap saving, and protocol filters. The capability is intentional and sensitive, although not inherently malicious.

semantic_findings.title: Plain HTTP Admin REST Examples
semantic_findings.description: The examples show RouterOS REST calls using admin credentials over http URLs. In non-lab environments, this can expose credentials and management traffic on the network.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples visibly use curl with admin authentication and http endpoints. The text appears lab-oriented, so the finding is medium rather than high.

content.value_statement: RouterOS packet capture setup is hard to remember during network debugging. This skill guides TZSP streaming, pcap saving, and receiver setup.
actual_capabilities: Explains RouterOS /tool/sniffer streaming and file capture modes.
Shows how to mirror selected flows with firewall mangle sniff-tzsp rules.
Describes Wireshark, tshark, and tcpdump receiver workflows for TZSP traffic.
Covers QEMU CHR lab setup details for host-side TZSP receiving.
Lists cleanup steps for sniffer settings and temporary mangle rules.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not authenticate to routers by itself.
Packet capture can expose sensitive data and needs authorization.
Some workflows require external tools such as Wireshark, tshark, tcpdump, or QEMU.
RouterOS behavior can differ by version, license, interface, and hardware offload state.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a RouterOS Connectivity Issue
use_cases.description: Capture ICMP, DNS, or TCP traffic to confirm whether packets reach the expected interface.

use_cases.title: Build a CHR Packet Lab
use_cases.description: Use QEMU CHR and TZSP streaming to reproduce protocol behavior without physical hardware.

use_cases.title: Collect Evidence for Incident Triage
use_cases.description: Mirror a narrow traffic flow to Wireshark or tshark for authorized investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me capture ICMP traffic on a RouterOS interface and save it as a pcap file.

prompt_templates.title: Stream TZSP to a Receiver
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate live analysis with a host receiver.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through streaming RouterOS sniffer output to a tshark receiver on my workstation.

prompt_templates.title: Mirror One Flow with Mangle
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted capture for a specific source, protocol, or port.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized sniff-tzsp mangle workflow for one host and explain how to remove it afterward.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CHR Debugging Lab
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced lab workflow using QEMU CHR and REST setup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a RouterOS CHR packet capture lab with TZSP streaming, receiver validation, and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: I need to see whether DNS queries leave a RouterOS bridge.
output: A focused capture plan using a DNS filter and a clear start and stop point.
A receiver checklist for Wireshark or tshark on the default TZSP port.
Cleanup notes for removing temporary capture settings.

output_examples.input: I want to mirror one client to tshark for five minutes.
output: A narrow mangle-based mirroring plan for the selected client address.
A reminder to confirm authorization before collecting packet payloads.
A verification checklist that confirms packets arrive at the receiver.

output_examples.input: My CHR lab is not sending TZSP packets to the host.
output: A troubleshooting path for QEMU host addressing, receiver binding, and port selection.
Likely causes such as wrong receiver IP, host firewall rules, or missing sniffer start state.

best_practices: Capture only the minimum traffic needed for the investigation.
Use authorized lab or production windows before enabling packet mirroring.
Stop captures and remove temporary mangle rules after testing.
anti_patterns: Do not capture broad production traffic without approval.
Do not leave TZSP receivers or firewall openings enabled after debugging.
Do not share pcap files before checking for credentials or private data.

faq.question: Does this skill run packet captures automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example workflows for authorized users.

faq.question: Which tools can receive TZSP traffic?
faq.answer: Wireshark and tshark can decode TZSP. tcpdump can verify raw UDP packet arrival.

faq.question: Can it save captures on the RouterOS device?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers sniffer file output and later download for analysis.

faq.question: Can it mirror only one flow?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes firewall mangle sniff-tzsp rules for targeted mirroring.

faq.question: Does hardware offload affect captures?
faq.answer: Yes. Hardware-offloaded bridge traffic may not be visible to the sniffer.

faq.question: Is packet capture sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. Captures can include credentials, payloads, and private network metadata.
